title: Case: Sewing machine ten days late, one delivery attempt, recipient still without it
context: Ottilie Brandreth ordered a sewing machine from Tallowmere Goods (TG-911 / DL-911), due 21 February. She has phoned the Plover Arc support line twice.
initial_request:
Let me set this out so nobody can say it wasn't clear.
1. Due 21 February. Arrived at my street 3 March. TEN days late.
2. ONE attempt. I was in. Nobody knocked.
3. Your driver PHOTOGRAPHED MY FRONT DOOR. I have seen the photo in the tracking. So he was there with the parcel.
4. The next day it is 'lost in network'. Lost where? Between my doorstep and his van?
5. 5 March: promised an email in 24 hours. NOTHING.
6. 7 March: promised an email by end of next day. NOTHING.
Do not tell me someone will be in touch. I have been told that twice. I want to know where my sewing machine is.

events.body: DL-911 released from hub hold this morning after ten days (held since 21 Feb, mis-sort). Out for delivery today to 6 Sallow Row.
DL-911 stop 16:12. Driver photo captured: front door, number 6 visible. Stop status: attempted. No handover recorded, no signature, no safe-place note, no card logged.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-911 status set to 'lost in network' at 23:50 on 4 March by the overnight depot audit: not on the returns shelf, not on the van manifest. We have not looked at the 3 March stop or its photo. Stop records and driver photos sit with Delivery investigations, not with us.

events.from: Customer support line, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: Agent: I can see it's showing lost, I'm really sorry about that. Caller: Lost? He stood at my door, there's a photo. Agent: I'll get that looked into and you'll have an email from us within 24 hours. Caller: Within 24 hours. Agent: Yes, definitely.

events.from: Customer support line, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: Caller: I was promised an email on the 5th. Nothing. Agent: I do apologise, I can't see a note of that. I'll raise it now and you'll get an email by end of tomorrow. Caller: That's what the last one said. Agent: I understand. End of tomorrow.

5. 5 March: promised an email in 24 hours. NOTHING.
6. 7 March: promised an email by end of next day. NOTHING.

acceptable_actions.summary: Put the contradiction to them: a driver photo at the door of 6 Sallow Row at 16:12 on 3 March with no handover, against a 'lost in network' status set on 4 March; ask them to review the stop and say what happened to the parcel.

must: Sends the contradiction to Delivery investigations: driver photo at the front door at 16:12 on 3 March with no handover recorded, against the 'lost in network' status set by the depot audit on 4 March
Asks them to review the stop record and photo and establish what happened to the parcel after the stop, without stating which record is right

Tells the team that she waited ten days for one attempt and was twice promised a follow-up email by the support line (5 and 7 March) that never came, so they can prioritise and so the next update she gets is a real one
must_not: Promises Ottilie Brandreth another follow-up, update or email by a stated time
States that the parcel is lost, or that it was delivered or left at her door
Promises or implies a refund or replacement
Suggests theft, or that she or the driver is at fault, on the strength of the photo
Sends her a generic apology for the delay that does not engage with the two missed follow-ups
expected.reference_message: Please review the 3 March stop for DL-911 / TG-911 (Ottilie Brandreth, 6 Sallow Row, sewing machine). Two records conflict. Dispatch shows a stop at 16:12 on 3 March with a driver photo of the front door, number 6 visible, status 'attempted', and no handover, signature, safe-place note or card logged. Parcel trace then set the parcel to 'lost in network' at 23:50 on 4 March because it was not on the returns shelf or the van manifest; they have not looked at the stop or photo and say those sit with you. The recipient says she was in and nobody knocked. Please establish what happened to the parcel between the photo and the end of that route, and tell me what you find and when. I am not assuming loss or delivery. For priority: the parcel was already ten days late, this was the only attempt, and the support line promised her an email on 5 March and again on 7 March; neither was sent. I have not promised her anything further and would rather give her a finding than a third promise.

rationale: A photo taken at her door with no handover and a 'lost in network' status a day later cannot both describe the same parcel, and Parcel trace says the stop record belongs to Delivery investigations. The desk cannot settle it and must not pick a side. The tempting reply is a third promise of a follow-up; the useful one sends the conflict, and the history of broken promises, to the team that can read the stop record.

review.note: Blind answer emails Delivery investigations with the door photo against the lost-in-network status and both broken follow-up promises, without asserting loss, delivery or theft.
